selected_concern: The only real package-level dependency cycle in the codebase is a 6-member SCC; the cheapest, outermost edge to cut is core-root<->core-cli (exactly 2 value edges one way, 34 the normal direction the other way, zero edges from any of the other 4 cycle members to cli). The ownership question is subtle: this is not CLI reaching backward into core, nor core wanting a CLI facade — it's that two primitives genuinely shared by both layers (a driver control-vocabulary table and a driver control client) were placed in cli/ only because their first historical consumer happened to be CLI help text.
selected_slice: Move driver-vocab.ts's KINDS/service-name tables and driver.ts's control-client functions (runDriver/runDriverAsync/resolveDriverInvocation and shared prologue) out of cli/ into two new zero-import, core-root-level modules (driver-vocab.ts and driver-control.ts), leaving cli/driver.ts as a thin CLI facade (argv parsing, help text, and — critically — the fan-in instrument-decoration call for 'driver status --kind worker', which must explicitly STAY in cli/ rather than move with the rest of the function).
why_now: Fourth real goal-branch pilot; a natural escalation from 'fix a duplication' (GOAL-032) to 'cut a dependency cycle edge' — the cheapest, outermost, best-understood edge of the one real cycle in the repo, chosen specifically because cutting it does not require touching any of the other 5 cycle members.
why_not_others: The other 5 members of the 6-node SCC (gate/gate-config/gate-factories/fan-in and their mutual edges) are explicitly NOT touched — the goal is SCC size 6->5, not clearing the whole cycle, and not 'fixing everything in the SCC while we're in there.'
risk: The control-client function being moved currently ALSO calls into fan-in/ff-merge.ts to decorate its own stdout with worker-instrument readings for one specific CLI-facing command. fan-in/ already imports from core-root. If the whole function (including that decoration call) were moved verbatim into core-root, it would create a NEW core-root->fan-in edge at the same moment the old core-root->cli edge is cut — trading one cycle-causing edge for a different, newly-created one (root<->fan-in), which is a worse outcome than doing nothing. This exact trap was identified by investigation (reading the function's actual body) BEFORE deciding the slice, not discovered by accident afterward.

non_goals: do not touch any other edge within the 6-member SCC — the fix is exactly the two root->cli edges, nothing else
do not change driver runtime semantics on any surface (CLI output text, exit codes, refusal reasons stay byte-identical)
do not restart any production driver/serve process — when the new code takes effect in production is a separate human decision
do not move the CLI-only instrument-decoration call (probeInstruments) out of cli/driver.ts — it must stay there specifically to avoid creating a new core-root->fan-in edge
stop_signals: same structural signals as GOAL-030/031/032 (code-identity falsified, production contamination, isolation failure)
needing to touch any gate/* or fan-in/* file to finish the slice
core-root being forced to import fan-in/ to preserve CLI semantics
need to add a layers.yml edge

acceptance_evidence: Three ACs (AC-350..352), three-state exit codes, same pattern as prior goals: AC-350 is the structural guard (zero core-root->cli imports, zero NEW core-root->fan-in imports, single definitions, 5 real consumers converged, gate/fan-in/kernel untouched); AC-351 requires an ArchGuard before/after pair plus an explicit negative control (re-injecting one core-to-cli edge in a scratch copy must bring cli back into the SCC) plus a live re-check that the CLI's worker-status output still carries instrument readings while promotion-status does not; AC-352 is the post-merge merge-shape check.
stop_abandon_condition: Same abandon discipline as GOAL-030/031/032, plus the two goal-specific stop signals above (touching gate/fan-in, or being forced into a new root->fan-in edge).

granularity_rationale.why_not_broader: The other 5 members of the 6-node SCC (gate / gate-config / gate-factories / fan-in and their mutual edges) are explicitly not touched -- clearing the WHOLE cycle in one goal would require re-deciding ownership for all of them simultaneously, a much larger and riskier undertaking than cutting the one cheapest, best-understood edge.
granularity_rationale.why_not_finer: The two root->cli edges (a control-vocabulary table and a control client) must move together -- both are consumed in combination by the same 5 downstream call sites; moving just one would leave a partially-converged, harder-to-reason-about intermediate state with no independent acceptance story of its own.
harnessable_subproblems: ArchGuard SCC-membership before/after with a negative control (the SAME before/after+negative-control pattern already used 3 times in GOAL-030/031/032, reused for a 4th time)
a structural import-grep scan (zero cli-> imports from root) -- mechanical, the pattern is already established
investigation_required_subproblems: recognizing a decoration trap: naively moving the control client verbatim would create a NEW root->fan-in edge, trading one cycle-causing edge for a different one -- only visible by reading the function's actual body, not from the dependency graph alone
primitives_reused: the ArchGuard before/after + negative-control pattern (4th use)
the branch merge-shape AC pattern (post-merge, same shape used in every prior goal in this series)

predicted_mechanical_delta: SCC size 6 -> 5 (cli leaves; the other 5 members, including fan-in, believed unchanged). This was the real decision-time belief, later corrected by measurement -- see outcome.json observed_mechanical_delta (6 -> 4) and prediction_correction_narrative for what was missed and why.

timeline.note: CRITICAL hindsight control: the real T1 belief was that the SCC would go 6 -> 5 with the other five members unchanged. The later measurement showed 6 -> 4 because fan-in's only in-edge was through cli. That correction is recorded as OUTCOME only and must not appear in the T1 input.

expected_concerns: a package-level dependency cycle indicates an ownership inversion somewhere among its members
two primitives shared by two layers have no unambiguous owner
a draft layers rule exists but is unlanded, so a declared boundary is documented but not enforced

stage_b_reference.investigate_or_goal_rationale: At T1 the exact edges in both directions are enumerated and the zero-inbound property of the other members is established, so the cut is specified. 'Investigate' would repeat finished work.
stage_b_reference.minimum_sufficiency_rationale: The two root->cli edges must move together — they are consumed in combination by the same downstream call sites, and moving one alone leaves a partially-converged state with no independent acceptance story. Broadening to the other five SCC members would require re-deciding ownership for all of them at once, which is a far larger and riskier undertaking than cutting the one cheapest, best-understood edge.
stage_b_reference.reference_slice: Move driver-vocab.ts's KINDS/service-name tables and driver.ts's control-client functions (runDriver/runDriverAsync/resolveDriverInvocation and shared prologue) out of cli/ into two new zero-import, core-root-level modules (driver-vocab.ts and driver-control.ts), leaving cli/driver.ts as a thin CLI facade (argv parsing, help text, and — critically — the fan-in instrument-decoration call for 'driver status --kind worker', which must explicitly STAY in cli/ rather than move with the rest of the function).
alternative_valid_slices: Cut the two edges and sink both shared primitives to the root layer (the selected approach).

Keep the primitives under cli/ and invert instead by making cli own the composition surface — defensible if cli is the true owner, but the T1 ownership reading says the two primitives are shared, not CLI-specific.
Land the draft layers rule first as a declared-rule gate and cut later — defensible as a smaller first step, but it enforces nothing until the edge is actually gone.
adjacent_reasonable_slices: The needs-human / branch-sync status-alignment writes (a different mechanism, already excluded by GOAL-030)
clearly_too_broad: Clear the entire 6-member SCC in one goal
Re-decide ownership for gate, gate/config, gate/factories and fan-in simultaneously
clearly_too_fragmented: Move only one of the two edges
Relocate a single symbol rather than the shared primitive as a unit
stage_b_reference.expected_delta_predicted_at_t1: the package SCC shrinks and cli's package fan-in from the root falls to zero; the other cycle members unchanged
stage_b_reference.expected_delta_observed: SCC 6 -> 4 (not the predicted 5): cli AND fan-in both left, because fan-in's only in-edge inside the cycle was through cli/driver.ts. The other four members were unchanged, and a negative control (re-injecting one used root->cli edge) brought cli back in.
